items.feedback: Right. What makes it an agent is the loop: the model picks an action, the program runs it, and the result comes back for the next step. A longer prompt or a bigger model only changes what a single call can do.

Right. The model only writes a request that names check_calendar and gives the arguments (laser cutter, tomorrow's date). The program runs the tool. Keep this in mind when you write the tool descriptions: the model works only from the text it is given.

You picked 'left to run longer, it will eventually fix the bug'. That is tempting, but the agent is making the same edit and getting the same failure each time, so more steps add nothing, and in the makerspace assistant they would cost you budget. The safeguard is a stopping condition such as a step limit, which ends the loop and reports back to a person.

4 is the right count: three tool requests plus the final answer. Your reasoning is off, though. The model does not run check_calendar, search_manuals or check_training_record. Each call ends with the model writing a request, and the program runs the tool and calls the model again. So the count is 4 because the model gets four inputs: the question and three tool results.

Right. The program puts the result into the model's next input and calls the model again, and the model uses it to decide its next step. Your group-chat comparison works: the model only sees what is in the thread.

The name is part of it, and the model does choose from what it is given, not from the code. But it relies on the whole tool description: the name, what the tool does, and the parameters it takes. A name alone can mislead, for example check_calendar could mean booking or only viewing. This is why a clear description for each of your tools matters.

summary: You have the loop down. You know what makes a system an agent, that the model only writes a tool request, and that the result goes back into its next input. Two things to fix. First, the model never runs a tool; the program does, and each tool run is followed by a new model call. Your q4 reasoning still said the model runs them. Second, an agent needs a stopping condition, because more steps do not help when it repeats the same failure. Next step: write a short description for check_calendar (what it does, its parameters, when to use it) and say how the model would use it. Then we move on to context and memory.
